title: Developing an in-Line method to improve mechanical and flame retardancy performance of polyethylene fiber
authors: Beyzanur Gunaydin; Aybeniz Seyhan; Yusuf Polat; Ali Kilic; Ali Demir; Mustafa Erdem Ureyen; Huseyin Avci
source_version: Publisher version of record, official fulltext HTML and publisher-provided indexed original PDF text
composition: ASPUN 6000 linear low-density polyethylene from Dow Chemical Company; melt flow index 19 g/10 min; density 0.935 g/cm³. In-line surface treatment with Aflammit PCO-900, source-described as pentaerythritol ester of phosphoric acid.
TGA_specimen_preparation: Approximately 10 mg of the identified phosphorus-containing fiber state in an open alumina pan. Cutting, grinding, additional conditioning and gas flow are unreported. Methods state heating to 800 °C, whereas thermal-results prose calls 600 °C the end of analysis; canonical endpoint is left blank. Table 1 reports residue specifically at 600 °C.
source_material_form_TGA_raw: Thermal properties method and Table 1 explicitly describe control and phosphorus-containing fibers.
LOI_method: TS 11162 EN ISO 4589; Concept Equipment, UK oxygen index device
LOI_specimen_preparation: Source reports specimens 80 mm long × 10 mm wide × 4 mm thick and explicitly calls Table 2 results fiber samples. How the fibers were assembled or held to these dimensions is not specified. No bundling, pressing, melting, molding, knitting or weaving is inferred.
source_numeric_evidence_description: Original Table 1 gives T10%, numerical residue at 600 °C and TDTGmax; original Table 2 gives measured LOI by zone II temperature and take-up speed. Only temperature/speed combinations identifying one Table 1 fiber state are proposed.
TG_locator: Table 1, printed p 8; Thermal properties results pp 8–9
LOI_locator: Table 2, printed p 9; Limiting oxygen index analysis pp 8–9; Figure 4 caption p 10
conditions_locator: Materials and fiber spinning pp 3–5; FR treatment preparation p 5; TG/DTG and LOI methods pp 5–6; hot drawing separation pp 11–13
source_location: Complete official publisher HTML through methods, Tables 1–5, conclusion and all 31 references. Publisher-provided original PDF text confirms printed pp 3–13 and Table 1 p 8 / Table 2 p 9. PDF bytes and figure pixels unavailable; no visual inspection claimed.
washing_state: Initial in-line treated fiber; no durability wash or separate post-treatment rinse assigned
treatment_chemistry: Aflammit PCO-900 organic phosphorus flame retardant in zone II water-based ARK4010 medium; zone I uses lower-viscosity water-based ARK8010.
source_bath_concentration_raw: 1.5 wt.% phosphorus / organic phosphorus in zone II; commercial PCO-900 separately reported to contain 24 wt.% phosphorus. Concentration basis retained as source wording, not converted to elemental P loading, retained coating mass or fiber add-on.
source_conditioning_raw: Mechanical test subsection says all treated and untreated fibers stored for at least 24 h in laboratory conditions. It does not explicitly assign this conditioning to TG or LOI, so no assay-specific conditioning is inferred.
limitations: Three uniquely mapped treated fiber states only, subject to independent source QA. LOI Table 2 omits zone II length: 25 °C/750 m/min, 50 °C/1000 m/min and 95 °C/1000 m/min each have exactly one corresponding state in Table 1 and Figure 5; this bounded cross-table assignment is explicit in pairing evidence. The two 50 °C lower-speed groups each contain 10 and 15 cm TG variants and are held because LOI does not distinguish them. Control TG at 2250 m/min conflicts with control LOI/MCC at 1000 m/min and is held. The source repeatedly calls both assays fiber tests, but assembly of the stated 80 × 10 × 4 mm LOI specimen is unreported and no geometry conversion is inferred. The bath concentration is source-labelled 1.5 wt.% phosphorus; no retained add-on or elemental concentration is calculated. Exact spinning temperature, post-bath drying, TG start temperature, gas flow, TG/LOI replicate counts and uncertainties are not stated. Subsequent hot-drawn or annealed states in Table 5 receive mechanical tests only and are not paired. The 24 h laboratory storage and at least ten specimens occur under mechanical/diameter methods and are not imported as TG/LOI replication. Source prose calls 21.5 the maximum across productions; specific Table 2 values are retained. A conclusion about the best MCC sample differs from MCC discussion, so no MCC data support these pairs. Public PDF and image retrieval failed; evidence-cache hashes are not PDF document hashes. Reference 30 is an earlier mechanical process paper; no unavailable numeric values or process temperatures are borrowed. Reference 21 original proceedings uses different ATH/APP masterbatch formulations and no PCO-900 zone bath, with no shared treated-state tuple found. Methods report a TG scan to 800 °C, but thermal-results prose explicitly calls 600 °C the end of analysis; both statements are retained and canonical TG_end_C is blank. Explicit R600 is supported independently within either range.
source_sample_label: Zone II 25 °C, 15 cm, take-up speed 750 m/min
sample_state: Initial PCO-900-treated LLDPE fiber spun through zone II at 25 °C over 15 cm at 750 m/min; before additional hot drawing
treatment_method: Produce LLDPE fibers on an industrial modified melt-spinning line with a 0.6 mm spinneret. Zone I uses lower-viscosity ARK8010 liquid over 160 cm at room temperature. Zone II uses higher-viscosity ARK4010 liquid with source-reported 1.5 wt.% phosphorus additive, adjusted to 25 °C and 15 cm fiber travel length. Take up at 750 m/min. The additive screening solutions were 10 wt.% stirred at 50 °C for one day; concentration was reduced for production, but the source does not specify a separate mixing schedule for the final bath. No subsequent hot drawing, washing or curing is assigned to the paired Table 1/2 state.
pairing_evidence: Table 2 identifies the treated fiber at 25 °C and 750 m/min with measured LOI 21.2; Table 1 has exactly one treated fiber with that temperature/speed, explicitly 15 cm, and gives T10 452 °C, TDTGmax 472 °C and residue 0.1% at 600 °C. Figure 5 caption enumerates the same produced fiber groups. Both assay sections and table captions identify fibers. The later mechanical subsection explicitly distinguishes hot drawing of previously produced fibers.
source_TGA_endpoint_raw: TG/DTG methods state heating up to 800 °C; thermal-results prose calls 600 °C the end of the analysis. These statements are unresolved. Table 1 explicitly reports residue at 600 °C, which remains valid within both ranges.
source_title: Developing an in-Line method to improve mechanical and flame retardancy performance of polyethylene fiber
